Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
40-year-old woman with 3-week history of left-sided hearing loss and facial numbness; occasional tinnitus and dizziness; suspected Bell’s palsy—referred for same-day in-person assessment.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Progressive reduced hearing in left ear and numbness over left ear/jawline for ~3 weeks.  
• Associated symptoms: Intermittent ringing (tinnitus) in left ear with occasional dizziness. No limb weakness/numbness, dysphagia, speech difficulty, visual changes, ear discharge, ear pain, pruritus, or fever.  
• Past medical history: Nasal polyps; remote episode of labyrinthitis; gastro-oesophageal discomfort (uses antacid).  
• Medications: Nasal spray for polyps (name/dose/route/frequency not documented); OTC Rennies antacid prn.  
• Allergies: Latex.  
• Family history: Brother with neurofibromatosis.  
• Social / preventive: Professional jockey; reduced training due to symptoms. Lives with partner (conflict noted—initially said lives alone). No pets.

Examination:
• No physical examination performed on video consult.  
• Vitals: not obtained.

Impression:
• Suspected Bell’s palsy causing unilateral facial sensory change and hearing symptoms; differential includes other otologic or neurological pathology.

Plan:
• Arrange same-day face-to-face GP clinic appointment for full neurological exam and otoscopy.  
• Doctor to message admin to book appointment; patient to phone support team in 5 minutes to confirm slot at convenient Central London site.  
• Reassured patient that condition not thought life-threatening but requires physical assessment today.  
• Will provide further explanation and management once diagnosis confirmed in clinic.

Quality checks:

● Missing expected elements: Objective physical exam, vitals, medication name/dose, allergy verification beyond latex, smoking/alcohol status.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient first stated living alone, later said lives with partner.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor repetitions, no significant inaudible sections.
